2027-02-02.title: The Presentation of the Lord
readings: The Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple
Who is this King of glory? The Lord of hosts, he is the King of glory
My eyes have seen your salvation, a light for revelation to the Gentiles
2027-02-02.alt: Feast. Blessing of candles and procession (or solemn entrance) before Mass. Gloria is said. World Day for Consecrated Life. Forty days after Christmas. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-02-02.verse: for my eyes have seen your salvation, which you have prepared in the presence of all peoples, a light for revelation to the Gentiles and for glory to your people Israel.”
theo: Malachi spoke to a tired people whose worship had grown careless, and promised: “See, I am sending my messenger to prepare the way before me, and the Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple.” But he warned: “who can endure the day of his coming… For he is like a refiner's fire and like fullers' soap.” Israel expected a king in glory. Today the promise is fulfilled in a way no one imagined: the Lord comes to his temple as a forty-day-old child, carried in his mother's arms, and the offering made for him is “a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons”, the offering of the poor.

Mary and Joseph come to fulfil the law: every firstborn son belongs to the Lord and must be presented to him, and the mother offers the sacrifice of purification. They come as ordinary, obedient, poor people. Yet the Spirit is at work. Simeon, “righteous and devout, looking forward to the consolation of Israel”, comes “guided by the Spirit” into the temple, takes the child in his arms, and sings: “Master, now you are dismissing your servant in peace… for my eyes have seen your salvation… a light for revelation to the Gentiles and for glory to your people Israel.” An old man holds the infant who holds the universe. The Church sings his song every night at Compline.

Then Simeon turns to Mary: “This child is destined for the falling and the rising of many in Israel, and to be a sign that will be opposed… and a sword will pierce your own soul too.” The light will be a light from the cross, and Mary will stand beneath it. Anna, a widow of eighty-four who “never left the temple but worshiped there with fasting and prayer night and day”, speaks of the child to all who were waiting. Hebrews explains why he came so low: “he had to become like his brothers and sisters in every respect, so that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest.” Today the Church blesses candles, because Christ is the light, and celebrates all consecrated men and women who, like Anna, give their whole lives to God.
conn: Forty days.
Leviticus 12 prescribed the mother's purification forty days after the birth of a son; Exodus 13 required the consecration of every firstborn.
The offering of the poor.
Leviticus 12:8 allows two turtledoves or two pigeons for those who cannot afford a lamb. Mary brings the offering of the poor, while carrying the true Lamb.
Hypapante.
The Greek name of the feast means “the Meeting”: the Lord meets his people in Simeon and Anna.
Nunc dimittis.
Simeon's song (Luke 2:29–32) is prayed every night in the Church's Night Prayer.
Candlemas.
From the fifth century in Jerusalem the feast was kept with lighted candles; candles blessed today are taken home for prayer, sickness and storms.
Consecrated life.
Since 1997 Pope St John Paul II made this day the World Day for Consecrated Life.
altar: The child presented in the temple is the same Lord offered on the altar. The temple of Jerusalem has become every church where the Mass is offered.
At Communion we, like Simeon, receive the Lord into our hands and hearts. Many priests pray the Nunc dimittis after Mass: now you dismiss your servant in peace.
outline: Light a candle and ask: what does a single flame do in a dark room?
Point 1 · The Lord comes to his temple
Malachi's promise fulfilled in a child.
Point 2 · The offering of the poor
Point 3 · A light for the nations
Point 4 · A sign opposed, a sword
Mary at the beginning of the cross.
An old man holding the infant who holds the world.
live: Bring your candle
Take home a blessed candle and light it at family prayer tonight.
Pray the Nunc dimittis
Pray Simeon's song (Luke 2:29–32) before sleep this week.
Honour consecrated life
Thank a religious sister, brother or priest for their life given to God.
Present yourself
Offer your day to God this morning, as Mary and Joseph offered Jesus.
fathers: St Sophronius of Jerusalem (in substance)
Let us all hasten to meet Christ with lighted candles; as the Virgin carried the true light, let us carry lights to show that he has come to enlighten us.
St Ambrose (in substance)
Simeon longed to be released from the body as from a prison; having seen the Lord, he asks to depart in peace, for he who sees Christ need not fear death.
magis: Marialis cultus 7
The Presentation is a joint commemoration of the Son and the Mother: the offering of Christ and the faith of Mary.
Vita consecrata 1, 16
Consecrated life as a total offering to God, a sign for the whole Church.
Catechism 529, 583
The Presentation shows Jesus as the firstborn belonging to the Lord; Simeon and Anna meet the Saviour.
Lumen gentium 57
Mary's union with her Son in the work of salvation, from the Presentation to the cross.
saints: Honoured in the Eastern Churches on 3 February as the God-receiver and the prophetess; models of patient, prayerful waiting.
2027-02-02.prayer: Almighty ever-living God, we humbly implore your majesty that, just as your Only Begotten Son was presented on this day in the Temple in the substance of our flesh, so, by your grace, we may be presented to you with minds made pure. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen.

2027-02-07.title: Fifth Sunday in Ordinary Time
readings: Nights of misery are apportioned to me
Praise the Lord, who heals the brokenhearted
Woe to me if I do not proclaim the gospel!
He cured many who were sick with various diseases
2027-02-07.alt: Year B. The last Sunday before Lent: Ash Wednesday falls on 10 February. 11 February, Our Lady of Lourdes, is the World Day of the Sick. Liturgical colour: green.
2027-02-07.verse: He came and took her by the hand and lifted her up. Then the fever left her, and she began to serve them.
theo: Job speaks for every sleepless sufferer: “Do not human beings have a hard service on earth…? I am allotted months of emptiness, and nights of misery are apportioned to me. When I lie down I say, ‘When shall I rise?’ But the night is long, and I am full of tossing until dawn.” And: “My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle, and come to their end without hope.” Scripture does not hide this cry; it places it in God's own Word. Job is not rebuked for complaining honestly. The Psalm answers him from far ahead: “He heals the brokenhearted, and binds up their wounds.” The God who “determines the number of the stars” also bends down to bandage a wound.

Mark shows us one day in Capernaum. Leaving the synagogue, Jesus enters the house of Simon and Andrew. Simon's mother-in-law lies in bed with a fever. “He came and took her by the hand and lifted her up. Then the fever left her, and she began to serve them.” Mark uses the same verb he will use for the resurrection: Jesus raises her. And her first act as a healed woman is service. By evening “the whole city was gathered around the door”, and Jesus heals many. Job's long night meets the dawn that comes to the door.

Then, “in the morning, while it was still very dark, he got up and went out to a deserted place, and there he prayed.” The healer draws his strength from the Father in the dark hours. When the disciples find him (“Everyone is searching for you”) he does not return to the easy success of yesterday: “Let us go on to the neighboring towns, so that I may proclaim the message there also; for that is what I came out to do.” Paul shares that same urgency: “woe to me if I do not proclaim the gospel!… I have become all things to all people, that I might by all means save some.” Healing, prayer and mission belong together. This week we begin Lent, and on Thursday we pray with the sick on the feast of Our Lady of Lourdes.
conn: Job.
The book wrestles with innocent suffering; it refuses easy answers and ends with an encounter with God, not an explanation.
Lifted her up.
Mark's verb (egeiren) is the verb of resurrection (Mark 16:6): every healing is a small Easter.
She began to serve.
The Greek diekonei gives us the word deacon; healing leads to service.
Peter's house.
At Capernaum archaeologists found a first-century house honoured by early Christians; an octagonal church was built over it, and a modern church now stands above.
Prayer in the dark.
Mark shows Jesus praying alone at three key moments: here, after feeding the five thousand (6:46), and in Gethsemane (14:35).
All things to all people.
Paul adapts everything except the Gospel itself, so that the message reaches every kind of person.
altar: Before Communion we pray: Lord, I am not worthy… but only say the word, and my soul shall be healed. The Lord who took a sick woman by the hand takes us by the hand at the altar.
Like Simon's mother-in-law, healed to serve, we are sent from Mass to serve: Go in peace, glorifying the Lord by your life.
outline: Ask: have you ever lain awake through a long night of pain or worry?
An honest cry in God's Word.
Point 2 · He took her by the hand
Point 4 · Woe to me if I do not proclaim
A whole town gathered at one door at sunset.
“He heals the brokenhearted, and binds up their wounds.”
live: Visit the sick (Mark 1:32)
Visit, call or pray with a sick person this week, especially before the World Day of the Sick.
Pray early
Like Jesus, give God the first minutes of the day before the noise begins.
Serve from your healing
Thank God for one healing in your life by serving someone today.
Prepare for Lent
Decide this week what you will pray, fast and give in Lent.
fathers: St Jerome (in substance)
May the Lord come to our house and touch our hand, so that the fever of sin may leave us; and when we are healed, let us rise at once and serve.
St Gregory the Great (in substance)
Job's sufferings were not a punishment but a testing; in his patience the holy man foreshadowed the Lord who would suffer for us.
magis: Salvifici doloris 26, 30
Christ gives meaning to suffering from within, and the Good Samaritan calls us to stop beside every sufferer.
Catechism 1503–1505
Christ the physician, who takes our infirmities upon himself.
Catechism 2602
Jesus often prays alone, in solitude, at night.
Evangelii gaudium 20–24
A Church that goes forth to every town and every person.
saints: 8 Feb: St Jerome Emiliani; St Josephine Bakhita (day of prayer against human trafficking). 10 Feb: Ash Wednesday, day of fasting and abstinence. 11 Feb: Our Lady of Lourdes (commemoration), World Day of the Sick. 14 Feb: First Sunday of Lent.
2027-02-07.prayer: Keep your family safe, O Lord, with unfailing care, that, relying solely on the hope of heavenly grace, they may be defended always by your protection. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. Let us also pray: Lord Jesus, you took the sick by the hand and lifted them up. Come to all who lie awake in pain tonight; heal the brokenhearted, raise us to serve, and make us eager to bring your message to every town. Amen.

2027-02-14.title: First Sunday of Lent
readings: God's covenant with Noah, set free from the waters of the flood
Your ways, O Lord, are love and truth to those who keep your covenant
Baptism, which this prefigured, now saves you
He was tempted by Satan, and the angels waited on him
2027-02-14.alt: Year B. The Rite of Election of catechumens for Easter Baptism is celebrated today in many dioceses. The memorial of Sts Cyril and Methodius is not kept this year because it falls on Sunday. No Gloria. Liturgical colour: violet.
2027-02-14.verse: And the Spirit immediately drove him out into the wilderness. He was in the wilderness forty days, tempted by Satan; and he was with the wild beasts; and the angels waited on him.
theo: Every First Sunday of Lent takes us into the desert with Jesus, but each year tells it differently. Mark, in Year B, is the briefest of all: two verses. “And the Spirit immediately drove him out into the wilderness. He was in the wilderness forty days, tempted by Satan; and he was with the wild beasts; and the angels waited on him.” No dialogue, no list of temptations. Just the scene: the Son, newly anointed at the Jordan, sent by the Spirit into the place of testing. He is the new Israel, who spent forty years in the wilderness and failed; he is the new Adam, who was tempted in a garden and fell. Jesus is tempted in a wilderness and stands firm. And the wild beasts around him and the angels serving him recall paradise restored: the harmony of creation that Isaiah foresaw, when “the wolf shall live with the lamb.”

The first reading opens with another new beginning. After the flood, God makes a covenant not only with Noah and his family but “with every living creature”: “never again shall all flesh be cut off by the waters of a flood.” As its sign he sets his bow in the clouds: “When I bring clouds over the earth and the bow is seen in the clouds, I will remember my covenant.” The bow, once a weapon of war, now hangs unstrung in the sky, pointed away from the earth. It is a sign of God's peace. St Peter sees in the flood a figure of baptism: in the ark “eight persons, were saved through water. And baptism, which this prefigured, now saves you.” Christ, “put to death in the flesh, but made alive in the spirit”, has suffered “for sins once for all, the righteous for the unrighteous, in order to bring you to God.”

After the desert Jesus comes into Galilee proclaiming: “The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has come near; repent, and believe in the good news.” This is Lent in one sentence. Today in cathedrals the catechumens who will be baptized at Easter are chosen and enrolled: the Rite of Election. For them Lent is the final preparation for the waters; for the rest of us, it is a return to the waters we have already passed through. The Psalm gives our prayer: “Make me to know your ways, O LORD; teach me your paths.” We do not go into this desert alone. The Spirit leads us, the angels serve us, and the One who was tempted in every way as we are, yet without sin, goes before us.
conn: Forty days.
Noah's rain fell forty days (Genesis 7:12); Moses fasted forty days on Sinai (Exodus 34:28); Elijah walked forty days to Horeb (1 Kings 19:8); Israel wandered forty years (Deuteronomy 8:2).
Drove him out.
Mark's strong verb (ekballō) is the same used for casting out demons: the Spirit thrusts Jesus into the battle with Satan.
The wild beasts.
Only Mark mentions them; they recall Adam among the animals and Isaiah's vision of peace (Isaiah 11:6–9).
The bow.
The Hebrew word for rainbow is the same as for a war bow; God hangs up his weapon as a sign of peace.
Eight persons.
The early Church saw the eighth day, the day of resurrection, in the eight saved in the ark; many ancient baptisteries are eight-sided.
The Rite of Election.
On this Sunday the bishop chooses the catechumens for Easter sacraments; their names are written in the Book of the Elect.
altar: The Lord who was fed by angels in the desert now feeds us with the Bread of Angels for our forty days.
Baptism brought us through the waters; the Eucharist sustains us on the journey to Easter, when we will renew our baptismal promises.
outline: Ask: what is a rainbow a sign of for you?
Point 1 · The bow in the clouds
God's covenant of peace with all creation.
Wild beasts at peace and angels serving.
“The time is fulfilled… repent, and believe in the good news.”
live: Enter the desert (Mark 1:12)
Choose a daily time of silence this Lent, even ten minutes, without phone or noise.
Remember your baptism
Find the date of your baptism, and thank God for it with holy water this week.
Pray for the elect
Pray daily for the catechumens preparing for Baptism at Easter.
Resist one temptation
Name your strongest temptation and ask Jesus for strength each time it comes.
fathers: St Augustine (in substance)
In Christ you were tempted, and in him you overcame. He took to himself our temptation so as to give us his victory; if in him we are tempted, in him we conquer the devil.
St Ambrose (in substance)
The flood was a figure of baptism: sin was drowned, the just were saved, and the dove brought the olive branch of peace, as the Spirit descends on the baptized.
St Gregory the Great (in substance)
It was not unworthy of our Redeemer to be tempted, for he came to be killed; he overcame our temptations by his own, as he overcame our death by his death.
magis: Catechism 538–540
The temptations of Jesus: the new Adam who remained faithful; Lent unites us to his forty days.
Catechism 56–58, 71
The covenant with Noah: God's covenant with all the nations.
Catechism 1219, 1094
The ark of Noah as a prefiguring of salvation by Baptism.
Catechism 2846–2849
Lead us not into temptation.
Rite of Christian Initiation of Adults 118–137
The Rite of Election on the First Sunday of Lent.
saints: Sts Cyril and Methodius (not kept this year)
Brothers from Thessalonica, apostles of the Slavs, co-patrons of Europe; they gave the Slavs the Scriptures and liturgy in their own tongue.
15–20 Feb: Lenten weekdays. 17 Feb: Seven Holy Founders of the Servite Order (commemoration). 21 Feb: Second Sunday of Lent; St Peter Damian not kept. 22 Feb: Chair of St Peter (feast).
2027-02-14.prayer: Grant, almighty God, through the yearly observances of holy Lent, that we may grow in understanding of the riches hidden in Christ and by worthy conduct pursue their effects. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. Let us also pray: Lord Jesus, you went into the desert, were tempted and overcame. Lead us by your Spirit through these forty days; keep us faithful to our baptism; strengthen the elect who will be baptized at Easter; and bring us all to the joy of your resurrection. Amen.

2027-02-01.title: Monday of the Fourth Week in Ordinary Time
readings: Through faith they conquered kingdoms; of them the world was not worthy
Be strong, and let your heart take courage, all you who wait for the Lord
Come out of the man, you unclean spirit!
2027-02-01.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 4 (Year I). Liturgical colour: green.
2027-02-01.verse: But Jesus refused, and said to him, “Go home to your friends, and tell them how much the Lord has done for you, and what mercy he has shown you.”
theo: Hebrews closes its great roll call of faith almost out of breath: “time would fail me to tell of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, of David and Samuel and the prophets.” Some, through faith, “shut the mouths of lions, quenched raging fire, escaped the edge of the sword”. Others “were tortured, refusing to accept release, in order to obtain a better resurrection”; they were stoned, sawn in two, homeless, “destitute, persecuted, tormented… of whom the world was not worthy.” Faith does not always look like victory. Some escaped the sword and some died by it, and both were faithful. The chapter ends with a surprise: they “did not receive what was promised, since God had provided something better so that they would not, apart from us, be made perfect.” The saints of the Old Covenant wait to be completed together with us in Christ.

The Gospel takes us across the lake into pagan country, to a man no one could bind. He lived among the tombs, “always howling and bruising himself with stones.” When Jesus asks his name, the answer is terrible: “My name is Legion; for we are many.” Evil divides and multiplies; it tears a person into pieces. Jesus speaks one word and the man is found “sitting there, clothed and in his right mind.” Strangely, the townspeople are afraid and beg Jesus to leave; they prefer their pigs to their healed neighbour. The healed man wants to follow Jesus, but Jesus sends him home: “Go home to your friends, and tell them how much the Lord has done for you, and what mercy he has shown you.” He becomes the first missionary to the Decapolis.
outline: Ask: who are the people of faith you remember in your own family?
Point 1 · The cloud of the faithful
Some escaped, some suffered; all believed.
The healed man becomes a missionary.
“Tell them how much the Lord has done for you.”
live: Remember the faithful (Hebrews 11:38)
Pray today for a grandparent or elder whose faith carried yours.
Tell your story (Mark 5:19)
Tell one person at home something the Lord has done for you.
2027-02-01.prayer: Lord Jesus, Son of the Most High God, you freed the man whom no chain could hold and sent him home to tell of your mercy. Free us from all that divides and torments us, and make us witnesses at home of what you have done for us. Amen.
altar: At Mass we pray with the whole cloud of witnesses, Abel, Abraham, the prophets and the martyrs. They are made perfect together with us in Christ.

2027-02-03.title: Wednesday of the Fourth Week in Ordinary Time · St Blaise; St Ansgar
readings: The Lord disciplines those whom he loves
The steadfast love of the Lord is from everlasting to everlasting on those who fear him
Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary?
2027-02-03.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 4 (Year I). Liturgical colour: green. Optional memorials: St Blaise, bishop and martyr (the blessing of throats is given today); St Ansgar, bishop. If a memorial is kept, the colour is red (St Blaise) or white (St Ansgar).
2027-02-03.verse: Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary and brother of James and Joses and Judas and Simon, and are not his sisters here with us?” And they took offense at him.
theo: Hebrews speaks to Christians who were tired of suffering: “In your struggle against sin you have not yet resisted to the point of shedding your blood.” It quotes Proverbs: “My child, do not regard lightly the discipline of the Lord, or lose heart when you are punished by him; for the Lord disciplines those whom he loves.” Hardship is not a sign that God has abandoned us; it can be the training of a Father who is making his children holy. “Now, discipline always seems painful rather than pleasant at the time, but later it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness.” So: “lift your drooping hands and strengthen your weak knees… Pursue peace with everyone, and the holiness without which no one will see the Lord,” and let “no root of bitterness” spring up.

In the Gospel Jesus comes home to Nazareth, and his own people stumble over his ordinariness: “Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary?” They know his trade, his mother and his relatives, and so they think they know him. “And they took offense at him.” Familiarity becomes a wall. Mark says something astonishing: “he could do no deed of power there, except that he laid his hands on a few sick people and cured them. And he was amazed at their unbelief.” God does not force himself on us. The same danger is ours: to think we already know Jesus because we have heard of him since childhood. Today the Church remembers St Blaise, bishop and martyr, whose blessing of throats asks God to protect us from illness and every evil; and St Ansgar, the patient missionary of the North, who preached for decades with little visible success.
outline: Ask: is it harder to listen to a stranger or to someone you know well?
Point 1 · The discipline of a Father
Point 2 · Is not this the carpenter?
God does not force his way in.
“The Lord disciplines those whom he loves.”
live: Lift drooping hands (Hebrews 12:12)
Encourage someone who is tired of a long struggle.
See Jesus afresh
Read Mark 6:1–6 slowly and ask: where have I taken Jesus for granted?
2027-02-03.prayer: Father of spirits, you train us as your children for our good, that we may share your holiness. Keep us from bitterness and from the unbelief that takes your Son for granted. Through the prayers of St Blaise, protect us from every illness of body and soul. Amen.
altar: The Lord who came to Nazareth in an ordinary carpenter comes to us in ordinary bread and wine. Faith alone recognises him; let familiarity never make us careless at the altar.

2027-02-04.title: Thursday of the Fourth Week in Ordinary Time
readings: You have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God
We ponder your steadfast love, O God, in the midst of your temple
He began to send them out two by two
2027-02-04.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 4 (Year I). Liturgical colour: green. In India many dioceses, especially in Tamil Nadu, honour St John de Britto, Jesuit priest and martyr (1693), today.
2027-02-04.verse: He called the twelve and began to send them out two by two, and gave them authority over the unclean spirits.
theo: Hebrews contrasts two mountains. At Sinai Israel met God in “a blazing fire, and darkness, and gloom, and a tempest, and the sound of a trumpet”, so terrifying that “Moses said, ‘I tremble with fear.’” But Christians have come somewhere else: “you have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to innumerable angels in festal gathering, and to the assembly of the firstborn who are enrolled in heaven… and to Jesus, the mediator of a new covenant, and to the sprinkled blood that speaks a better word than the blood of Abel.” Abel's blood cried out for vengeance; the blood of Jesus speaks forgiveness. This is what happens at every Mass: we stand with angels and saints at the festival of heaven.

In the Gospel Jesus “called the twelve and began to send them out two by two, and gave them authority over the unclean spirits.” They go in pairs, because witness is never solitary. They travel light: “nothing for their journey except a staff; no bread, no bag, no money in their belts.” They depend on God and on the hospitality of those who receive them. Their message is simple, “that all should repent”, and their works are signs of the Kingdom: “They cast out many demons, and anointed with oil many who were sick and cured them.” The Church sees in that anointing the beginning of the sacrament of the Anointing of the Sick. Mission is not a privilege of a few; every baptized Christian is sent.
outline: Ask: what would you pack if you had to leave with only a staff and sandals?
Point 3 · Travel light, heal the sick
Trust and signs of the Kingdom.
“He began to send them out two by two.”
live: Join the festival (Hebrews 12:22)
At your next Mass, remember that the angels and saints are worshipping with you.
Go two by two
Invite a friend to join you in one act of service this week.
2027-02-04.prayer: Lord Jesus, mediator of the new covenant, you send your disciples two by two with nothing but trust. Free us from the baggage that holds us back, and send us to call others to repentance and to bring your healing. Amen.
altar: At every Mass we come to Mount Zion and the city of the living God; the sprinkled blood of Jesus speaks a better word than the blood of Abel.

2027-02-05.title: Saint Agatha, Virgin and Martyr
readings: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever
The Lord is my light and my salvation
John, whom I beheaded, has been raised
2027-02-05.alt: Memorial. Friday of the Fourth Week in Ordinary Time (Year I). Liturgical colour: red.
2027-02-05.verse: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.
theo: Hebrews ends with practical counsel for a community under pressure: “Let mutual love continue. Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers, for by doing that some have entertained angels without knowing it. Remember those who are in prison, as though you were in prison with them.” It asks that marriage be honoured, that lives be kept “free from the love of money”, and gives the reason for courage: “he has said, ‘I will never leave you or forsake you.’ So we can say with confidence, ‘The Lord is my helper; I will not be afraid.’” And then one of the great verses of Scripture: “Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.” The Lord who strengthened the martyrs is the same Lord who walks with us.

Mark tells the death of John the Baptist with a sharp eye. Herod “feared John, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man… he liked to listen to him.” Yet at a drunken birthday banquet, trapped by a rash oath and by what his guests would think, he orders the prophet's head brought on a platter. Herod is not a monster; he is a weak man who knows the truth and will not obey it. John, in prison, is the free one. Today we honour St Agatha of Catania in Sicily, a young woman martyred about the year 251 because she refused to give herself to a powerful official and would not deny Christ. Like John, she chose truth over survival. Her name is spoken in the First Eucharistic Prayer, and Christians have prayed to her for centuries in sickness and danger.
outline: Ask: have you ever done something wrong because of what others would think?
Point 2 · The same yesterday, today, forever
“Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.”
live: Show hospitality (Hebrews 13:2)
Welcome a stranger or newcomer at church or work today.
Choose truth
Refuse one small compromise you would make only to please others.
2027-02-05.prayer: May the Virgin Martyr Saint Agatha implore your compassion for us, O Lord, we pray, for she found favour with you by the courage of her martyrdom and the chastity of her life. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen.
altar: St Agatha's name is spoken in the Roman Canon, among the martyrs with whom we offer the Sacrifice. The Christ she died for is the same Christ on our altar today.

2027-02-06.title: Saints Paul Miki and Companions, Martyrs
readings: May the God of peace, who brought back from the dead the great shepherd of the sheep, make you complete
The Lord is my shepherd, I shall not want
They were like sheep without a shepherd
2027-02-06.alt: Memorial. Saturday of the Fourth Week in Ordinary Time (Year I). Liturgical colour: red.
2027-02-06.verse: As he went ashore, he saw a great crowd; and he had compassion for them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd; and he began to teach them many things.
theo: Hebrews closes with an invitation and a blessing. The invitation: “Through him, then, let us continually offer a sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of lips that confess his name. Do not neglect to do good and to share what you have, for such sacrifices are pleasing to God.” The old temple sacrifices are over; now our praise and our sharing become the offering. The blessing is one of the most beautiful in the New Testament: “Now may the God of peace, who brought back from the dead our Lord Jesus, the great shepherd of the sheep, by the blood of the eternal covenant, make you complete in everything good so that you may do his will.”

In the Gospel the apostles return from their mission and tell Jesus everything. He says: “Come away to a deserted place all by yourselves and rest a while.” Jesus cares for tired workers. But the crowd runs ahead of them, and when Jesus sees them, “he had compassion for them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd; and he began to teach them many things.” Rest gives way to compassion. Today we honour St Paul Miki, a Japanese Jesuit, and his twenty-five companions, priests, brothers, catechists and lay people, among them young boys, who were crucified on a hill at Nagasaki on 5 February 1597. From his cross Paul Miki preached to the crowd and forgave his executioners. For more than two centuries Japanese Christians kept the faith in secret without priests, until missionaries returned in the nineteenth century and found them still praying. The Good Shepherd had not left his flock.
outline: Ask: when you are exhausted, what do you most need?
Lips that confess, hands that share.
Compassion, and the martyrs of Nagasaki.
live: Rest with Jesus (Mark 6:31)
Take fifteen quiet minutes today alone with the Lord.
Pray for the persecuted
Pray for Christians in Asia who suffer for their faith.
2027-02-06.prayer: O God, strength of all the Saints, who through the Cross were pleased to call the Martyrs Saint Paul Miki and companions to life, grant, we pray, that by their intercession we may hold with courage even until death to the faith that we profess. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen.
altar: Every Mass is the sacrifice of praise through Christ. The martyrs of Nagasaki, crucified like their Lord, show us what it means to offer our bodies with his.

2027-02-08.title: Monday of the Fifth Week in Ordinary Time
readings: God said: Let there be light; and there was light
May the Lord be glad in his works
All who touched even the fringe of his cloak were healed
2027-02-08.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 5 (Year I). Liturgical colour: green. Optional memorials of St Jerome Emiliani or St Josephine Bakhita (white). Today is also the International Day of Prayer and Awareness against Human Trafficking.
2027-02-08.verse: And wherever he went, into villages or cities or farms, they laid the sick in the marketplaces, and begged him that they might touch even the fringe of his cloak; and all who touched it were healed.
theo: The weekday readings now open the Bible at its first page: “In the beginning when God created the heavens and the earth, the earth was a formless void and darkness covered the face of the deep.” Into that darkness God speaks: “Let there be light”; and there was light. Day by day the formless becomes ordered: light and darkness, sky and sea, dry land and plants, sun, moon and stars. Again and again we hear the refrain: “And God saw that it was good.” Creation is not an accident or a battle of gods, as the neighbouring peoples imagined; it is the free gift of one good God who speaks and it is done. The sun and moon that others worshipped are simply lamps hung by God to mark the seasons.

The Gospel shows the same creative goodness at work in Jesus. When he lands at Gennesaret, the people recognize him at once and rush about the whole region, carrying the sick on mats to wherever they hear he is. In villages, cities and farms they lay the sick in the marketplaces and beg “that they might touch even the fringe of his cloak; and all who touched it were healed.” The Word through whom all things were made now walks among his creatures, and his touch restores what sin and sickness have marred. Today the Church may honour St Josephine Bakhita, the Sudanese slave girl who found in Christ “a Master” who loved her, and became a Canossian sister. In her the Creator's goodness was restored to a life that cruelty had tried to destroy.
outline: Ask: when did you last stop to look at a sunrise and thank God?
God speaks and creation comes to be.
Creation is a gift, not a god.
Point 3 · The fringe of his cloak
live: Look and give thanks (Psalm 104:24)
Spend two minutes today looking at one created thing and praising God for it.
Bring the sick to Jesus
Pray by name for one sick person, or visit or call them.
2027-02-08.prayer: Lord God, Creator of light and of all that is good, you spoke and the world came to be, and in your Son you touch and heal what is broken. Open our eyes to the goodness of your works, bring our sick to the fringe of his cloak, and through the prayers of St Josephine Bakhita set free all who are held in slavery. Amen.
altar: Bread and wine, “fruit of the earth and work of human hands”, are brought to the altar. The good things of creation become the Body and Blood of the One through whom all things were made, and we touch far more than the fringe of his cloak.

2027-02-09.title: Tuesday of the Fifth Week in Ordinary Time
readings: Let us make humankind in our image, according to our likeness
O Lord, our Sovereign, how majestic is your name in all the earth!
You abandon the commandment of God and hold to human tradition
2027-02-09.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 5 (Year I). Liturgical colour: green. Tomorrow is Ash Wednesday, the beginning of Lent, a day of fasting and abstinence.
2027-02-09.verse: So God created humankind in his image, in the image of God he created them; male and female he created them.
theo: The creation account reaches its summit. After the fish and birds and animals, God says something new: “Let us make humankind in our image, according to our likeness.” Only of the human being is this said. “So God created humankind in his image, in the image of God he created them; male and female he created them.” Every person, rich or poor, born or unborn, healthy or disabled, carries the image of God. Man and woman together reflect him, and they receive a task: to fill the earth and care for it as God's stewards. Then comes the seventh day: God “rested on the seventh day from all the work that he had done. So God blessed the seventh day and hallowed it.” Our work finds its meaning in rest and worship.

The Psalm marvels: “what are human beings that you are mindful of them…? Yet you have made them a little lower than God, and crowned them with glory and honor.” But the Gospel shows how that glory can be emptied. The Pharisees criticise the disciples for eating without the ritual washing of hands. Jesus answers with Isaiah: “This people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me.” They had let human customs smother God's command, even using the vow of “Corban” to avoid supporting their parents. “You abandon the commandment of God and hold to human tradition.” On the eve of Lent the question is pointed: is my religion a matter of the lips, or of the heart that bears God's image?
outline: Ask: what makes a human being precious?
Tradition that serves God, not replaces him.
live: Honour God's image (Genesis 1:27)
Treat one person you usually overlook with special respect today.
Prepare for Lent
Decide tonight on one act of prayer, one of fasting and one of almsgiving for Lent.
2027-02-09.prayer: God our Creator, you made us in your image and crowned us with glory and honour. Keep us from honouring you with our lips while our hearts are far from you. As Lent begins, turn our hearts back to you and teach us to see your image in every person. Amen.
altar: At Mass we are not only lips that speak but bodies that kneel and hearts that are offered. The Eucharist restores in us the image of God that sin has dimmed.

2027-02-10.title: Ash Wednesday
readings: Rend your hearts and not your clothing
Have mercy, O Lord, for we have sinned
Be reconciled to God. See, now is the acceptable time
Your Father who sees in secret will reward you
2027-02-10.alt: Beginning of Lent. Day of fasting and abstinence (universal law: abstinence from meat from age 14; fasting, one full meal, from 18 to 59; follow the norms of your diocese). Ashes are blessed and given after the homily. The Gloria and the Alleluia are omitted from today until Easter. The memorial of St Scholastica is not kept this year. Liturgical colour: violet.
2027-02-10.verse: Yet even now, says the LORD, return to me with all your heart, with fasting, with weeping, and with mourning; rend your hearts and not your clothing.
theo: Lent opens with a trumpet. A locust plague had stripped the land of Judah bare, and the prophet Joel saw in it a call to conversion: “Yet even now, says the LORD, return to me with all your heart… rend your hearts and not your clothing.” The tearing of garments was the old sign of grief; God asks for something deeper, a heart torn open to him. And the reason is not fear but his own character: “for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love.” Joel calls everyone, the elders and the infants, the bride and the bridegroom, the priests weeping “between the vestibule and the altar”. Lent is not private self-improvement; it is the whole Church returning together.

St Paul turns the call into a plea: “we entreat you on behalf of Christ, be reconciled to God.” The ground of our reconciliation is astonishing: “For our sake he made him to be sin who knew no sin, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.” The sinless Son took our place, so that we might take his. And there is urgency: “See, now is the acceptable time; see, now is the day of salvation!” Not someday. Now. The ashes we receive are not a mark of gloom but of honesty: we are dust, and to dust we shall return, yet the dust that God loves can be raised to glory.

In the Gospel Jesus names the three great works of Lent: almsgiving, prayer and fasting. He does not abolish them; he purifies them. “Beware of practicing your piety before others in order to be seen by them.” Give alms so quietly that your left hand does not know what your right hand is doing. Pray in your room with the door shut. Fast with your face washed and your head anointed. Three times we hear the promise: “your Father who sees in secret will reward you.” The paradox of today is plain: we go out with a cross of ash on our foreheads, yet Jesus warns us against showing off. The ash is not to be admired; it is a confession that we are sinners in need of mercy, and an invitation to a hidden life of love that only the Father sees.
conn: Ashes.
From palm branches of last year's Palm Sunday, burned and blessed. In the Old Testament dust and ashes were signs of repentance (Jonah 3:6; Job 42:6).
The two formulas.
“Repent, and believe in the Gospel” (Mark 1:15) or “Remember that you are dust, and to dust you shall return” (cf. Genesis 3:19).
Forty days.
Noah's flood, Moses on Sinai, Elijah's journey to Horeb, Nineveh's forty days and Jesus' forty days in the desert stand behind Lent.
Rend your hearts.
Tearing garments was a public sign of grief (Genesis 37:34); Joel asks for the inward reality.
Made him to be sin.
Paul does not mean Christ sinned, but that he bore the full weight and consequence of our sin (cf. Isaiah 53:6).
Three works.
Almsgiving toward neighbour, prayer toward God, fasting toward oneself: the three directions of conversion.
altar: We receive ashes and then come to the altar. The one who knew no sin gives himself to sinners; Lent begins at the table of mercy.
The Eucharistic fast before Communion, small as it is, teaches the larger lesson of Lent: we hunger first for him.
outline: Hold up a pinch of ash and ask: what is left when a palm branch burns?
Return to the God who is gracious.
Point 2 · Now is the acceptable time
An ash cross on a child's forehead.
“Return to me with all your heart.”
live: Fast and abstain today
Keep the Church's fast and abstinence; offer your hunger for someone in need.
Choose three works
One act of prayer, one of fasting, one of almsgiving, kept every day of Lent.
Go to confession
Plan to receive the sacrament of Reconciliation in the first week of Lent.
Give in secret (Matthew 6:3–4)
Set aside what you save by fasting for the poor, and tell no one.
fathers: St Peter Chrysologus (in substance)
Prayer, fasting and mercy are three things that are one and give life to each other: fasting is the soul of prayer, and mercy is the lifeblood of fasting. Let no one separate them.
St Leo the Great (in substance)
What Christians should do at all times must now be done with greater care and devotion, so that the forty days may cleanse what the rest of the year has stained.
St Augustine (in substance)
Fasting and almsgiving are the two wings of prayer, by which it flies up to God.
magis: Sacrosanctum Concilium 109–110
Lent has a twofold character, baptismal and penitential; penance should be interior, individual and social.
Paenitemini (Paul VI, 1966)
The Church's teaching on penance and the days of fasting and abstinence.
Catechism 1434–1439
Fasting, prayer and almsgiving as forms of interior penance; the times of penance.
Catechism 540
By the forty days of Lent the Church unites herself to the mystery of Jesus in the desert.
Code of Canon Law 1249–1253
Ash Wednesday and Good Friday as days of fasting and abstinence.
saints: Sister of St Benedict, consecrated to God from childhood; her memorial, normally 10 February, gives way to Ash Wednesday.
11 Feb: Our Lady of Lourdes (commemoration; World Day of the Sick). 14 Feb: First Sunday of Lent; Sts Cyril and Methodius not kept this year.
2027-02-10.prayer: Grant, O Lord, that we may begin with holy fasting this campaign of Christian service, so that, as we take up battle against spiritual evils, we may be armed with weapons of self-restraint. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. Let us also pray: Father of mercy, we are dust, yet you love us. As we receive these ashes, tear open our hearts, teach us to pray in secret, to fast with joy and to give without counting, and bring us to Easter made new. Amen.

2027-02-11.title: Thursday after Ash Wednesday
readings: I have set before you life and death, blessings and curses. Choose life
Happy are they who hope in the Lord
Whoever loses his life for my sake will save it
2027-02-11.alt: Lenten weekday. The Gloria and the Alleluia are omitted throughout Lent. Liturgical colour: violet. Commemoration of Our Lady of Lourdes (its collect may be used). World Day of the Sick.
2027-02-11.verse: Then he said to them all, “If any want to become my followers, let them deny themselves and take up their cross daily and follow me.
theo: On the edge of the promised land Moses sets a choice before Israel: “See, I have set before you today life and prosperity, death and adversity.” To love the Lord, walk in his ways and keep his commandments is life; to turn away and bow to other gods is death. And Moses pleads: “Choose life so that you and your descendants may live, loving the LORD your God, obeying him, and holding fast to him; for that means life to you.” The Psalm paints the same two roads: the one who delights in the law of the Lord is “like trees planted by streams of water”, while the wicked are “like chaff that the wind drives away.” On the second day of Lent the Church places this choice before us too.

But Jesus reveals that the road to life passes through the cross. “The Son of Man must undergo great suffering, and be rejected… and be killed, and on the third day be raised.” Then he says to all: “If any want to become my followers, let them deny themselves and take up their cross daily and follow me.” Daily: not one heroic act, but the small faithful choices of each day. “For those who want to save their life will lose it, and those who lose their life for my sake will save it. What does it profit them if they gain the whole world, but lose or forfeit themselves?” Today, 11 February, we also remember Mary's appearing to St Bernadette at Lourdes in 1858. There Our Lady called for prayer and penance, and countless sick people have found healing or the grace to carry their cross. Mary, who stood by the cross of her Son, teaches us that the cross carried with Jesus leads to life.
outline: Ask: what is the most important choice you made this week?
The two ways set before us.
Point 2 · Take up your cross daily
The road to life passes through the cross.
Mary, the sick and the call to penance.
live: Choose life today (Deuteronomy 30:19)
Make one choice today for God's way when another way is easier.
Carry a cross with love
Accept one small daily cross without complaint, and offer it for the sick.
2027-02-11.prayer: Lord God, you set before us life and death and call us to choose life. Help us to deny ourselves, take up our cross daily and follow your Son. Through the prayers of Our Lady of Lourdes, comfort the sick and give them strength and healing. Amen.
altar: The cross we take up daily is joined at every Mass to the one sacrifice of Christ. With Mary at the foot of the cross, we offer our sufferings with his.

2027-02-12.title: Friday after Ash Wednesday
readings: Is not this the fast that I choose?
A broken and contrite heart, O God, you will not despise
When the bridegroom is taken away from them, then they will fast
2027-02-12.alt: Lenten weekday. The Gloria and the Alleluia are omitted throughout Lent. Liturgical colour: violet. Friday of abstinence: the Fridays of Lent are days of abstinence from meat.
2027-02-12.verse: Is not this the fast that I choose: to loose the bonds of injustice, to undo the thongs of the yoke, to let the oppressed go free, and to break every yoke?
theo: Isaiah is told to shout like a trumpet at a people who seem very religious. They seek God daily, they fast, they bow their heads, and they complain: “Why do we fast, but you do not see? Why humble ourselves, but you do not notice?” God's answer is blunt: “Look, you serve your own interest on your fast day, and oppress all your workers.” They fast and quarrel; they bow like a bulrush and lie on sackcloth, yet nothing changes in their treatment of others. Then the Lord describes the fast he wants: to loose the bonds of injustice, to let the oppressed go free, “to share your bread with the hungry, and bring the homeless poor into your house; when you see the naked, to cover them, and not to hide yourself from your own kin.” Fasting that does not lead to justice and mercy is an empty ritual.

Then comes the promise: “Then your light shall break forth like the dawn, and your healing shall spring up quickly… Then you shall call, and the LORD will answer; you shall cry for help, and he will say, Here I am.” In the Gospel the disciples of John ask why Jesus' disciples do not fast. Jesus answers with a wedding image: “The wedding guests cannot mourn as long as the bridegroom is with them, can they? The days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast.” Jesus is the Bridegroom of Israel, the God who wedded his people. Christian fasting is not gloomy self-punishment; it is the longing of the bride for the Bridegroom, whom we await, and a love that makes room for the poor. On this first Friday of Lent we abstain from meat and remember the day the Bridegroom was taken away on the cross.
outline: Ask: can someone fast and still be unjust?
Point 1 · Fasting that God does not see
Break the yoke, share your bread.
“Is not this the fast that I choose?”
live: Fast with justice (Isaiah 58:7)
Share a meal, or the money saved by fasting, with someone hungry.
Undo a yoke
Pay a worker fairly and promptly, or forgive a debt, or lighten someone's burden today.
2027-02-12.prayer: Lord God, you do not want empty fasting but hearts that set the oppressed free and share bread with the hungry. Make our Lenten fast a work of justice and love, a longing for your Son, the Bridegroom, and a light that breaks forth like the dawn. Amen.
altar: Every Friday recalls the day the Bridegroom was taken away. At Mass we receive him who gave his body for us, and we are sent to share our bread with the hungry.

2027-02-13.title: Saturday after Ash Wednesday
readings: If you offer your food to the hungry, your light shall rise in the darkness
Teach me your way, O Lord, that I may walk in your truth
I have come to call not the righteous but sinners to repentance
2027-02-13.alt: Lenten weekday. The Gloria and the Alleluia are omitted throughout Lent. Liturgical colour: violet.
2027-02-13.verse: Jesus answered, “Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick; I have come to call not the righteous but sinners to repentance.”
theo: Isaiah continues yesterday's teaching on true fasting with a cascade of promises. “If you remove the yoke from among you, the pointing of the finger, the speaking of evil, if you offer your food to the hungry and satisfy the needs of the afflicted, then your light shall rise in the darkness and your gloom be like the noonday.” Notice the small sins named: the pointing finger, the evil word. Lent is a time to give them up. And the promises are beautiful: “you shall be like a watered garden, like a spring of water, whose waters never fail”; you shall rebuild ancient ruins and be called “the repairer of the breach”. The reading ends with the sabbath: if you call it “a delight” and honour it, “then you shall take delight in the LORD.” Mercy to the neighbour and worship of God belong together.

In the Gospel Jesus sees Levi, a tax collector, sitting at his booth: a man despised as a collaborator and cheat. Jesus says only two words: “Follow me.” And Levi “got up, left everything, and followed him.” Then he throws a great banquet for Jesus, with a crowd of tax collectors and others. The Pharisees grumble: “Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?” Jesus answers: “Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick; I have come to call not the righteous but sinners to repentance.” Lent is not for the perfect; it is for the sick who know they need the Doctor. The first step is Levi's: to get up from the booth where we have been sitting too long, and to follow.
outline: Ask: who would be the last person you would expect Jesus to call?
The life God gives to the merciful.
Levi gets up and leaves everything.
“I have come to call… sinners to repentance.”
live: Stop pointing (Isaiah 58:9)
Give up criticism and gossip for one whole day.
Go to the Physician
Make an appointment for confession this week.
2027-02-13.prayer: Lord Jesus, Physician of souls, you called Levi from his tax booth and ate with sinners. Call us too, and give us the courage to get up and follow you. Take away from us the pointing finger and the evil word, and make us like a watered garden, a spring whose waters never fail. Amen.
altar: Levi's banquet was a feast of mercy with sinners. Every Mass is that feast: before Communion we confess, Lord, I am not worthy, and the Physician comes to the sick.

quick: Forty days after his birth Jesus is presented in the temple.
Simeon takes him in his arms: my eyes have seen your salvation.
He is a light for the nations and a sign that will be opposed.
2027-02-02.action: Light a blessed candle at family prayer tonight.
2027-02-02.question: Have I presented my whole life to God, or only parts of it?
catechism: The Presentation of Jesus in the temple.
kidsaint: Two old people who waited in the temple for many years to see God's promised Saviour. When Mary and Joseph brought baby Jesus, they knew him at once and praised God. Lesson: if we pray and wait, God lets us see him!
2027-02-02.special: Feast of the Presentation of the Lord (Candlemas). World Day for Consecrated Life.
term: The traditional English name of today's feast, from the blessing of candles. The candles remind us that Christ is the light of the world.

family.explain: Mary and Joseph brought baby Jesus to the temple. An old man named Simeon took him in his arms and thanked God, because he saw that this baby was the Saviour, the light for all people.
family.intention: We pray for all priests, sisters and brothers who have given their lives to God.
family.ask: Ask: “How can our family be a light for others this week?”

illus: An illustration

In a convent in Kollam an old sister, nearly ninety, could no longer teach or nurse. Each morning she sat in the chapel with a small candle beside her and prayed for every name the other sisters brought her. A young novice asked whether she missed working. She smiled: I am Anna now. I never leave the temple. Someone must keep the light burning while the others go out.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, light of the nations, you came to your temple in the arms of Mary. Come to us now and make us your light. Amen.
share: The Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple (Malachi 3:1). Am I seeking him?
My eyes have seen your salvation (Luke 2:30). Where have I seen God's salvation?
A sword will pierce your own soul too (Luke 2:35). What sorrow can I unite with Mary's?
pm.resp: Christ, light of the world, shine on us.
interc: For the Church, that she may carry Christ's light to all nations.
For all consecrated men and women, on their world day.
For the elderly who wait in faith, like Simeon and Anna.
For mothers and newborn children.
For our group, that we may offer our lives to God.
pm.close: Father, your Son was presented in the temple as the light of the nations. Purify our hearts and present us to you, burning with his light. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Job cries out in his long night of suffering.
Jesus takes a sick woman by the hand, lifts her up, and she serves.
Jesus prays in the dark and goes on to proclaim the message everywhere.
2027-02-07.action: Visit, call or pray with a sick person this week.
2027-02-07.question: Whose hand does Jesus want me to take this week?
catechism: The sacrament of the Anointing of the Sick.
kidsaint: A girl from Sudan who was kidnapped and sold as a slave, and treated very cruelly. Later she met Jesus, became free and became a religious sister in Italy. She forgave everyone and was always kind. Her feast is tomorrow. Lesson: Jesus can heal even the deepest hurts!
2027-02-07.special: Fifth Sunday in Ordinary Time. Last Sunday before Lent.
term: The sacrament in which a priest anoints the seriously ill or elderly with blessed oil, praying for strength, peace, forgiveness and, if God wills, healing of the body (James 5:14–15).

family.explain: Peter's mother-in-law was sick with a fever. Jesus took her hand and helped her up, and she was well! Then she got up and served everyone.
family.intention: We pray for all who are sick, and for doctors and nurses.
family.ask: Ask: “Who is sick that we can visit or pray for this week?”

illus: An illustration

A palliative-care nurse in Kottayam works night shifts with patients who cannot sleep for pain. She says many ask her the question of Job: when will this night end? She cannot always take away the pain. But she holds their hands, and some tell her that a hand held in the dark is the first time they have felt God near. She calls her work the Capernaum shift.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, healer of the sick and hope of the sleepless, take us by the hand and lift us up. Amen.
share: Nights of misery are apportioned to me (Job 7:3). Whom do I know who is living through a long night?
He took her by the hand and lifted her up (Mark 1:31). How has Jesus lifted me?
Woe to me if I do not proclaim the gospel (1 Corinthians 9:16). Do I feel any urgency to share my faith?
interc: For the sick, the dying and those in pain, especially before the World Day of the Sick.
For doctors, nurses and caregivers.
For those who suffer depression and sleepless nights.
For the Church as we prepare to begin Lent.
For our group, that healed by Christ we may serve.
pm.close: God of all consolation, your Son came to the door of every sufferer. Heal us, raise us, and send us to serve and to proclaim. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God set his bow in the clouds as a sign of his covenant with all creation.
The ark prefigured baptism, which now saves us through the risen Christ.
Jesus was tempted in the desert and proclaimed: repent, and believe.
2027-02-14.action: Choose a daily time of silence for the forty days.
2027-02-14.question: What is the desert God is leading me into this Lent, and what temptation must I face there?
catechism: The temptations of Jesus in the desert.
Noah's ark, a figure of Baptism.
kidsaint: Two brothers who went far away to tell people about Jesus. The people there had no letters to write their language, so the brothers made an alphabet and wrote the Bible for them! Lesson: we can help everyone hear about Jesus in a way they understand.
2027-02-14.special: First Sunday of Lent. Rite of Election. Sts Cyril and Methodius not kept this year.
term: Catechumens who have been chosen by the bishop at the Rite of Election, usually on the First Sunday of Lent, to receive Baptism, Confirmation and the Eucharist at the Easter Vigil.

family.explain: The Holy Spirit led Jesus into the desert for forty days. Satan tempted him, but Jesus said no to Satan. Wild animals were near, and angels took care of him. Then Jesus said: turn back to God and believe the good news!
family.intention: We pray for people who will be baptized at Easter.
family.ask: Ask: “When is it hard for us to say no to something wrong? Let us ask Jesus for help.”

illus: An illustration

A young mother in Thiruvalla was preparing for Baptism at Easter. On the First Sunday of Lent she stood before the bishop as her name was called and written in the Book of the Elect. She said afterwards: for months I felt alone in my desert of questions. Today I heard my name, and I knew the whole Church was walking with me to the water.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you were tempted in the desert and overcame. Lead us through our forty days by your Spirit. Amen.
share: I have set my bow in the clouds (Genesis 9:13). Do I trust God's covenant of peace?
Baptism… now saves you (1 Peter 3:21). How do I live my baptism?
He was in the wilderness forty days, tempted by Satan (Mark 1:13). What is my temptation?
pm.resp: Your ways, O Lord, are love and truth.
interc: For the elect, who will be baptized at Easter.
For all who face strong temptation.
For the care of creation, God's covenant partner.
For people in the deserts of loneliness, illness or doubt.
For our group, that we may keep a faithful Lent.
pm.close: Father, your Son was tempted and overcame. Make us strong in him through these forty days. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The heroes of faith suffered, yet they believed.
Jesus frees the man called Legion with one word.
The healed man is sent home to tell of God's mercy.
2027-02-01.action: Tell one person at home something the Lord has done for you.
2027-02-01.question: What does the Lord want me to tell my own family about his mercy?

family.explain: Jesus healed a man who was very sick in his mind. The man wanted to go with Jesus, but Jesus said: go home and tell your family what God has done for you!
family.intention: We pray for people who are troubled in their minds and hearts.
family.ask: Ask: “What good thing has God done for our family that we can thank him for?”

illus: An illustration

A young man from a coastal village near Alappuzha spent three years in the grip of alcohol and drugs. His mother said he was like a stranger who shouted at walls. After a retreat and long treatment he came home. The parish priest suggested he join a mission team in another town, but he said: first I must sit at my mother's table and let her see that God gave her son back. That was his first sermon.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are stronger than every evil that binds us. Make us whole and send us to tell of your mercy. Amen.
share: Of whom the world was not worthy (Hebrews 11:38). Whose faithfulness do I remember with gratitude?
My name is Legion; for we are many (Mark 5:9). What divides me inside?
Tell them how much the Lord has done for you (Mark 5:19). Whom should I tell?
pm.resp: Lord, have mercy on us and make us whole.
interc: For persecuted Christians, the faithful of whom the world is not worthy.
For those troubled in mind, and for their families.
For those bound by addiction.
For doctors, counsellors and priests who bring healing.
For our group, that we may witness first at home.
pm.close: Father, your Son sends the healed back to their homes as witnesses. Make our homes places where your mercy is told and seen. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God disciplines us as a Father, for our holiness.
Nazareth took offense at the carpenter, the son of Mary.
Unbelief closes the door to God's power.
2027-02-03.action: Encourage someone who is tired of a long struggle.
2027-02-03.question: Have I taken Jesus for granted because he is familiar?

family.explain: Jesus went home to Nazareth. The people said: he is only the carpenter, we know his mother! They did not believe, so Jesus could not do many miracles there.
family.intention: We pray for anyone who is sick, especially with a throat or chest illness, through St Blaise.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we listen to Jesus with new ears this week?”

illus: An illustration

A woman in Kozhikode had attended Mass every Sunday for forty years and admitted she rarely listened to the Gospel: she knew it already. During a long illness her grandson read the Gospels aloud to her each evening. She said afterwards: I had known Jesus the way the people of Nazareth knew the carpenter. In the hospital I met him for the first time.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, son of Mary, carpenter of Nazareth, open our eyes to see you as you are, and heal our unbelief. Amen.
share: The Lord disciplines those whom he loves (Hebrews 12:6). Can I see my hardships as training?
Is not this the carpenter? (Mark 6:3). Where do I take Jesus for granted?
He was amazed at their unbelief (Mark 6:6). What would amaze Jesus about my faith?
pm.resp: Lord, I believe; help my unbelief.
interc: For those whose struggles have made them tired or bitter.
For the sick, especially those with illnesses of the throat, through St Blaise.
For the Church in Scandinavia and northern Europe, through St Ansgar.
For families, that they may see Christ in the ordinary.
For our group, that we may listen with fresh hearts.
pm.close: Father, your Son was rejected in his own town. Give us faith that welcomes him every day. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: We have come not to frightening Sinai but to joyful Zion.
Jesus sends the Twelve two by two.
They travel light, call to repentance and heal the sick.
2027-02-04.action: Invite a friend to join you in one act of service this week.
2027-02-04.question: What baggage keeps me from going where Jesus sends me?

family.explain: Jesus sent his friends out in pairs to tell people about God. They did not take money or food, only a stick for walking. They trusted God to take care of them.
family.intention: We pray for missionaries all over the world.
family.ask: Ask: “Who could we visit together to bring them God's love?”

illus: An illustration

Two retired schoolteachers in a parish near Thiruvananthapuram began visiting housebound elderly people every Thursday. They took nothing but a small Bible and a bottle of water. One said: alone I would have given up after a month. Together we have kept going for six years. Jesus knew what he was doing when he sent them out in twos.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you send us out as you sent the Twelve. Give us courage, companions and trust. Amen.
share: You have come to Mount Zion (Hebrews 12:22). Do I see Mass as heaven's festival?
Two by two (Mark 6:7). Who is my companion in mission?
Nothing for their journey except a staff (Mark 6:8). What can I leave behind?
pm.resp: Lord, send us out in your name.
interc: For missionaries and catechists.
For the sick, and for priests who anoint them.
For those who travel far from home for work.
For the Church in India, through St John de Britto.
For our group, that we may serve together.
pm.close: Father, you sent your Son and he sent his apostles. Send us too, light and trusting, to bring your Kingdom near. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Let mutual love and hospitality continue.
Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today and forever.
Herod feared his guests; John and St Agatha feared only God.
2027-02-05.action: Welcome a stranger or newcomer today.
2027-02-05.question: Where do I act like Herod, knowing the truth but fearing what others think?

family.explain: God says: I will never leave you. Jesus is the same yesterday, today and forever. He was with St Agatha when she was brave, and he is with us too.
family.intention: We pray for women and girls who suffer violence, through St Agatha.
family.ask: Ask: “When is it hard for us to be brave for Jesus?”

illus: An illustration

A young woman working in a Bengaluru office was told by her manager that her promotion depended on spending a weekend away with him. She refused and was moved to a lesser post. A year later she said: I lost a title, but I kept myself. When I read about St Agatha I realised that saints are not only in old books.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are the same yesterday, today and forever. Give us the courage of St John the Baptist and St Agatha. Amen.
share: Do not neglect to show hospitality (Hebrews 13:2). Whom can I welcome?
I will never leave you or forsake you (Hebrews 13:5). Do I believe this?
Out of regard for his oaths and for the guests (Mark 6:26). Whose opinion rules me?
pm.resp: The Lord is my light and my salvation.
interc: For women and girls who suffer violence or harassment.
For those suffering from breast cancer and all who care for them, through St Agatha.
For prisoners, and for those who visit them.
For leaders, that they may not fear people more than truth.
For our group, that we may stand firm in faith.
pm.close: Father, you gave St Agatha courage to keep faith and purity unto death. Make us faithful in small things and great. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Offer God a sacrifice of praise and of sharing.
Jesus invites tired apostles to rest, then has compassion on the crowd.
St Paul Miki and companions died on crosses at Nagasaki, forgiving.
2027-02-06.action: Take fifteen quiet minutes alone with the Lord today.
2027-02-06.question: Do I make time to rest with Jesus, and do I have compassion for the crowd?

family.explain: The apostles were very tired, so Jesus said: come and rest. But many people came, and Jesus felt sorry for them because they were like sheep without a shepherd. So he taught them.
family.intention: We pray for Christians in Japan and all of Asia, through St Paul Miki.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we rest with Jesus this Sunday?”

illus: An illustration

A Japanese Catholic visiting Kerala told a parish youth group about her great-great-grandparents, hidden Christians near Nagasaki. For generations they baptised their babies secretly and prayed before a statue that looked like a Buddhist goddess but was really Mary. She said: we had no priests for two hundred and fifty years, yet the Shepherd kept us. Do not take your Sunday Mass for granted.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Good Shepherd, give us rest in you, compassion for others, and courage like the martyrs of Japan. Amen.
share: Let us continually offer a sacrifice of praise (Hebrews 13:15). Is my life a song of praise?
Come away… and rest a while (Mark 6:31). Do I let Jesus refresh me?
He had compassion for them (Mark 6:34). For whom should I have compassion?
pm.resp: The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.
interc: For Christians persecuted in Asia, through St Paul Miki and companions.
For the Church in Japan.
For pastors and all who are worn out in service.
For those who are like sheep without a shepherd.
For our group, that we may rest in Christ and serve with compassion.
pm.close: Father, you strengthened the martyrs of Nagasaki on their crosses. Make us faithful unto death and generous unto all. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
God saw that it was good.
All who touched the fringe of Jesus' cloak were healed.
2027-02-08.action: Pray by name for one sick person today.
2027-02-08.question: Do I see creation as God's gift, and do I bring my wounds to Jesus' touch?

family.explain: At the very beginning everything was dark. God said: Let there be light! And there was light. Everything God made is good.
family.intention: We pray for people who are sick, and for children who are not free.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing God made that you love? Let us thank him for it.”

illus: An illustration

A teacher in Alappuzha took her catechism class to the lake shore before dawn. They sat in silence until the sun came up over the water. Then she read slowly: God said, let there be light. A boy whispered: it is like watching the first day. She told them: every morning is God saying it again.

pm.open: Creator God, you spoke and there was light. Speak your light into our hearts tonight. Amen.
share: Let there be light (Genesis 1:3). Where do I need God's light?
God saw that it was good (Genesis 1:10). Do I thank God for his creation?
That they might touch even the fringe of his cloak (Mark 6:56). Whom can I bring to Jesus?
pm.resp: Lord, how manifold are your works!
interc: For the care of God's creation and for those who protect it.
For the sick in our parish and families.
For victims of human trafficking, through St Josephine Bakhita.
For doctors, nurses and caregivers.
For our group, that we may praise God in all things.
pm.close: Father, all your works are good. Heal what is broken in us and in the world, through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God created humankind in his image, male and female.
God blessed the seventh day and made it holy.
Jesus warns: honour God with the heart, not only the lips.
2027-02-09.action: Choose your three Lenten resolutions tonight.
2027-02-09.question: Is my faith only on my lips, or in my heart?

family.explain: God made people last, and he made us like himself! Every person is special because God's image is in them.
family.intention: We pray for people who are treated as if they are not important.
family.ask: Ask: “What will each of us do for Jesus this Lent?”

illus: An illustration

In a hospital ward in Kozhikode a nurse was asked why she spoke so gently to a patient who could no longer speak or move. She answered: my grandmother taught me that God's face is hidden in every face. This man is still God's image. He deserves my best words.

pm.open: Lord, you made us in your image. Turn our hearts back to you as Lent begins. Amen.
share: In the image of God he created them (Genesis 1:27). Do I see God's image in others?
God blessed the seventh day (Genesis 2:3). Do I keep Sunday holy?
Their hearts are far from me (Mark 7:6). Where is my heart far from God?
pm.resp: Lord, how majestic is your name!
interc: For respect for every human life from conception to natural death.
For married couples, that they may reflect God's image together.
For workers who have no day of rest.
For those who care for elderly parents.
For our group, that our Lent may be a true return of the heart.
pm.close: Father, crown us again with your glory, and make our worship true. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Return to the Lord with all your heart; rend your hearts, not your clothing.
Be reconciled to God; now is the acceptable time.
Give, pray and fast in secret; your Father sees and rewards.
2027-02-10.action: Keep today's fast and give what you save to the poor.
2027-02-10.question: What does God want me to change, from the heart, this Lent?
catechism: Interior penance and its many forms.
Lent and Jesus' forty days in the desert.
The precept of fasting and abstinence.
kidsaint: The twin sister of St Benedict. She loved to talk with God and about God. Once she prayed and a storm came so that her brother had to stay and keep talking about heaven with her! Lesson: Lent is a time to talk with God more.
2027-02-10.special: Ash Wednesday: beginning of Lent, day of fasting and abstinence, blessing and imposition of ashes.
term: Latin for “the fortieth”: the ancient name for Lent, the forty days of preparation for Easter, from Ash Wednesday to the Mass of the Lord's Supper on Holy Thursday.

family.explain: Jesus says: when you do good, do not show off. Give quietly, pray quietly in your room, and God your Father, who sees everything, will be happy with you.
family.intention: We pray that our whole family may grow closer to Jesus this Lent.
family.ask: Ask: “What will each of us give up, and what will each of us give, this Lent?”

illus: An illustration

A schoolboy in Kollam put his Lenten savings in a tin marked only with a cross. At Easter his mother found it heavy with coins and asked what it was for. He said: Father told us to give in secret, so I did not tell you. Together they took it to the parish for a family whose house had burnt down. The family never learnt who had given it.

pm.open: Lord, we are dust, yet you love us. Tear open our hearts and turn them to you this Lent. Amen.
share: Rend your hearts and not your clothing (Joel 2:13). What outward show do I hide behind?
Now is the acceptable time (2 Corinthians 6:2). What have I been postponing with God?
Your Father who sees in secret (Matthew 6:6). Do I do good to be seen?
pm.resp: Have mercy, O Lord, for we have sinned.
interc: For the whole Church, that this Lent may be a true return to God.
For catechumens preparing for Baptism at Easter.
For the hungry, who fast without choosing to.
For those far from God, that they may hear: be reconciled.
For our group, that we may pray, fast and give together.
pm.close: Father, gracious and merciful, receive our Lent and lead us to the joy of Easter. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God sets before us life and death: choose life.
Follow Jesus by taking up your cross daily.
Our Lady of Lourdes, health of the sick, pray for us.
2027-02-11.action: Accept one cross today without complaint, and offer it for a sick person.
2027-02-11.question: Which daily cross am I trying to avoid instead of carrying with Jesus?

family.explain: Jesus says: if you want to follow me, carry your cross every day. A cross can be doing a hard job without grumbling, or being kind when it is difficult.
family.intention: We pray for all sick people, through Our Lady of Lourdes.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one small cross each of us can carry for Jesus today?”

illus: An illustration

A retired bus conductor from Ernakulam went to Lourdes with a parish pilgrimage, hoping his damaged legs would be healed. They were not. But he came home saying: at the grotto I stopped asking why me. I saw hundreds of sick people praying for each other. I learnt to carry my cross with Jesus. That was my miracle.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you call us to take up our cross daily. Give us courage, and through your Mother comfort the sick. Amen.
share: Choose life (Deuteronomy 30:19). What choice is before me now?
Take up their cross daily (Luke 9:23). What is my daily cross?
What does it profit them? (Luke 9:25). What am I tempted to gain at the cost of my soul?
pm.resp: Mary, health of the sick, pray for us.
interc: For the sick, especially those who suffer alone.
For doctors, nurses and all who care for the sick.
For pilgrims at Lourdes and at Marian shrines in India.
For those facing a hard choice between right and wrong.
For our group, that we may carry our crosses with love this Lent.
pm.close: Father, your Son carried his cross to give us life. Help us to follow him with Mary. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God rejects fasting that ignores the poor and oppresses workers.
The true fast frees the oppressed and shares bread with the hungry.
We fast in longing for Jesus, the Bridegroom.
2027-02-12.action: Share a meal or the money saved by fasting with someone hungry.
2027-02-12.question: Does my fasting make me kinder and more just?

family.explain: God says: the best fasting is sharing food with hungry people, giving homes to people who have none, and giving clothes to people who need them.
family.intention: We pray for poor and hungry families.
family.ask: Ask: “What can our family share with someone in need this Lent?”

illus: An illustration

A parish youth group in Palakkad decided to skip their Friday snacks in Lent. Each week they cooked the money into a pot of rice and curry and took it to migrant workers at a construction site. One worker asked why. A girl answered: because God says the fast he likes is sharing bread. The worker said: then today your God has fed me.

pm.open: Lord, teach us the fast you choose: hearts that share and hands that set free. Amen.
share: Why do we fast, but you do not see? (Isaiah 58:3). Is my fasting only outward?
