To share your bread with the hungry (Isaiah 58:7). With whom can I share?
Then they will fast (Matthew 9:15). Do I fast out of love for Jesus?
pm.resp: A broken and contrite heart, O God, you will not despise.
interc: For the hungry and the homeless.
For workers who are underpaid or unpaid.
For those held in any kind of bondage.
For employers, that they may be just.
For our group, that our fasting may become sharing.
pm.close: Father, make our fasting a light that breaks forth like the dawn. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Remove the pointing finger and the speaking of evil.
The merciful will be like a watered garden.
Jesus came to call sinners: Levi got up and followed.
2027-02-13.action: Give up criticism and gossip for one whole day.
2027-02-13.question: Where am I still sitting at my tax booth, unwilling to get up and follow?

family.explain: Levi took money unfairly, and people did not like him. But Jesus said: follow me! Levi left everything and had a big party for Jesus. Jesus is like a doctor who comes for sick people.
family.intention: We pray for people who feel too bad to come back to God.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone we have been unkind about? How can we be kind to them?”

illus: An illustration

A man in Kannur had not been to church for thirty years and ran a shop known for cheating customers. One Lent the parish priest stopped at his counter, bought something and said: come and see me, I want to talk. The man came. After confession he began paying back customers he had cheated. He said: I thought the Church was for good people. Then I learnt it is a hospital.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Doctor of our souls, you came for sinners. We come to you as we are. Heal us. Amen.
share: The pointing of the finger, the speaking of evil (Isaiah 58:9). Whom do I criticise?
You shall be like a watered garden (Isaiah 58:11). Where do I need God's water?
He got up, left everything, and followed him (Luke 5:28). What must I leave?
pm.resp: Teach me your way, O Lord.
interc: For sinners who feel unwelcome in the Church.
For those who hear confessions, that they may be ministers of mercy.
For tax collectors and all in public finance, that they may be honest.
For people who criticise and those who are hurt by criticism.
For our group, that we may welcome sinners as Jesus did.
pm.close: Father, your Son ate with sinners. Seat us at his table and heal us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, through the prophet Malachi God promised: the Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple (Malachi 3:1). Israel expected a king in glory. Today the Lord comes to his temple as a little child, carried in his mother's arms.

Mary and Joseph come to fulfil the law. They bring the offering of the poor, a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons (Luke 2:24). The one who will be the true Lamb is redeemed with the gift of the poor. God enters our world through humility and obedience.

Simeon, guided by the Spirit, takes the child in his arms and sings: Master, now you are dismissing your servant in peace… for my eyes have seen your salvation (Luke 2:29–30). An old man holds the One who holds the universe. That is why we carry candles today: Christ is a light for revelation to the Gentiles.

But Simeon also tells Mary: this child is destined for the falling and the rising of many… and a sword will pierce your own soul too (Luke 2:34–35). The light will shine from the cross. Mary offers her Son today and will offer him again on Calvary.

Anna, a widow of eighty-four, never left the temple but worshiped there with fasting and prayer night and day (Luke 2:37). Today we thank God for all consecrated men and women who, like Anna, give their whole lives to him.

Hebrews says he became like us in every respect, so that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest (Hebrews 2:17). Let us present ourselves to him today, and carry his light into every dark place. Amen.
kids: Children, Mary and Joseph took baby Jesus to God's house. Old Simeon held him and said: this baby is the light for the whole world!
When you see a candle in church, remember: Jesus is our light. Let us shine for him.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, Job speaks for everyone who has lain awake in pain: when I lie down I say, ‘When shall I rise?’ But the night is long, and I am full of tossing until dawn (Job 7:4). God's Word does not hide this cry. It gives words to our suffering.
The Psalm answers: he heals the brokenhearted, and binds up their wounds (Psalm 147:3). The God who counts the stars bends down to bandage a wound.

In the Gospel, Jesus enters Simon's house. Simon's mother-in-law lies with a fever. He came and took her by the hand and lifted her up. Then the fever left her, and she began to serve them (Mark 1:31). Healed, she serves. Every grace we receive is meant to become service.

By evening the whole city was gathered around the door (Mark 1:33). And before dawn, while it was still very dark, Jesus went out to a deserted place, and there he prayed (Mark 1:35). The healer draws his strength from the Father in the dark.

When the disciples say everyone is searching for you, he answers: let us go on to the neighboring towns, so that I may proclaim the message there also (Mark 1:38). Paul says: woe to me if I do not proclaim the gospel! (1 Corinthians 9:16).

This week Lent begins, and on Thursday we pray with the sick on the feast of Our Lady of Lourdes. Let us take someone by the hand: visit the sick, pray in the early hours, and share the Good News. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus held the hand of a sick lady and helped her up, and she was well! Then she helped everyone else.
Let us pray for sick people this week, and maybe visit someone who is sick with Mummy or Daddy.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, every First Sunday of Lent takes us into the desert with Jesus. This year Mark tells it in just two verses: the Spirit immediately drove him out into the wilderness. He was in the wilderness forty days, tempted by Satan; and he was with the wild beasts; and the angels waited on him (Mark 1:12–13).

Israel was tested forty years in the wilderness and failed. Adam was tested in a garden and fell. Jesus, the new Adam and the true Israel, is tested and stands firm. And around him are wild beasts at peace and angels serving: a glimpse of paradise restored.

In the first reading God makes a covenant with Noah and with every living creature, and sets his bow in the clouds as a sign (Genesis 9:13). The bow, a weapon of war, now hangs in the sky as a sign of peace.

St Peter tells us that the ark, in which eight persons were saved through water, prefigured baptism, which now saves you (1 Peter 3:20–21). Christ suffered for sins once for all, the righteous for the unrighteous, to bring us to God. Today the elect, who will be baptized at Easter, are called by name.

Then Jesus proclaims: the time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has come near; repent, and believe in the good news (Mark 1:15). That is Lent in one sentence: turn around, and trust the good news.

We do not enter this desert alone. The Spirit leads us, the angels serve us, and Jesus, who was tempted as we are, goes ahead of us. Let us pray with the Psalm: make me to know your ways, O LORD. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus stayed in the desert for forty days. Satan tried to make him do wrong, but Jesus said no! Angels came to help him.
When you are tempted to do something wrong, say: Jesus, help me! He will help you say no.

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews closes its list of the heroes of faith: time would fail me to tell of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, of David and Samuel and the prophets (Hebrews 11:32). Some shut the mouths of lions; others were tortured, stoned and killed by the sword.
Faith does not always look like victory. Some escaped and some died, and all were faithful: people of whom the world was not worthy (Hebrews 11:38). And they wait to be made perfect together with us.

In the Gospel Jesus meets a man whom no chain could hold, living among the tombs. His name is Legion, for we are many (Mark 5:9). Evil tears a person into pieces. One word of Jesus, and the man sits clothed and in his right mind (Mark 5:15).

He wants to follow Jesus, but Jesus says: go home to your friends, and tell them how much the Lord has done for you (Mark 5:19). Our first mission field is our own home. Let us tell our families of his mercy. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus made a very sick man well, and then said: go home and tell your family what God has done for you! Tonight, tell your family one good thing God did for you today.

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews tells a tired community: my child, do not regard lightly the discipline of the Lord, or lose heart when you are punished by him; for the Lord disciplines those whom he loves (Hebrews 12:5–6). Our hardships are not signs that God has left us.

Discipline always seems painful rather than pleasant at the time, but later it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness (Hebrews 12:11). So lift your drooping hands, pursue peace, and let no root of bitterness spring up.

In Nazareth the people said: is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary? And they took offense at him (Mark 6:3). They thought they knew him, so they could not receive him. He could do no deed of power there, and he was amazed at their unbelief.

We too can take Jesus for granted because we have known him since childhood. Today, through the prayers of St Blaise, let us ask for healing of body and soul, and ask for new eyes to see the Lord. Amen.
kids: Children, the people of Nazareth said: he is only the carpenter! They did not believe in Jesus. Let us always listen to Jesus as if we are hearing him for the first time.

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews tells us we have not come to Sinai with its fire, darkness and trumpet. You have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to innumerable angels in festal gathering (Hebrews 12:22).
We have come to Jesus, the mediator of a new covenant, and to the sprinkled blood that speaks a better word than the blood of Abel (Hebrews 12:24). Every Mass is this festival of heaven.

In the Gospel Jesus called the twelve and began to send them out two by two (Mark 6:7). They took nothing but a staff. They preached repentance, cast out demons, and anointed with oil many who were sick and cured them (Mark 6:13).
We too are sent, not alone but together, not loaded with baggage but trusting in God. Let us go from this Mass two by two to bring his healing. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus sent his friends out in pairs to help people and tell them about God. Who can you go with to do something kind this week?

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews says: let mutual love continue. Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers, for by doing that some have entertained angels without knowing it (Hebrews 13:1–2). Remember prisoners, honour marriage, keep free from the love of money.
Why can we live like this? Because he has said: I will never leave you or forsake you (Hebrews 13:5). Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever (Hebrews 13:8).

In the Gospel Herod liked to listen to John, yet out of regard for his oaths and for the guests he ordered his death (Mark 6:26). He knew the truth but feared people more than God. John, in chains, was the free man.

Today we honour St Agatha, the young martyr of Sicily, who chose Christ over safety and purity over the will of a powerful man. The Christ who strengthened her is the same today. Let us ask for her courage. Amen.
kids: Children, St Agatha was a brave girl who loved Jesus more than anything. Even when she was hurt, she stayed faithful. Jesus helps us to be brave too!

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews says: through him, then, let us continually offer a sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of lips that confess his name (Hebrews 13:15). And do not neglect to do good and to share what you have.

It blesses us: may the God of peace, who brought back from the dead our Lord Jesus, the great shepherd of the sheep… make you complete in everything good so that you may do his will (Hebrews 13:20–21).

In the Gospel Jesus tells his tired apostles: come away to a deserted place all by yourselves and rest a while (Mark 6:31). But seeing the crowd, he had compassion for them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd (Mark 6:34).

Today we honour St Paul Miki and his companions, crucified at Nagasaki in 1597. From the cross Paul Miki preached and forgave. Let us rest in the Good Shepherd and, like the martyrs, give our lives with compassion. Amen.
kids: Children, St Paul Miki and his friends in Japan, even young boys, loved Jesus so much that they died on crosses, singing and forgiving. Let us pray for children everywhere who suffer for Jesus.

homily: Dear friends, today we begin to read the first page of the Bible: in the beginning when God created the heavens and the earth (Genesis 1:1). Darkness covered the deep, and God said: let there be light; and there was light (Genesis 1:3).

Day after day God gives order and life, and again and again we hear: God saw that it was good. Creation is not a god to be feared or worshipped; it is a gift from the one good God. Even the sun and moon are lamps he has hung in the sky.

In the Gospel the people of Gennesaret run through the whole region bringing their sick to Jesus. They beg to touch even the fringe of his cloak, and all who touch it are healed (Mark 6:56). The Word who made all things now walks among us and heals.

Today we may remember St Josephine Bakhita, sold as a child slave, who found in Jesus a Master who loved her. Let us thank God for his creation, bring our sick to Jesus, and pray for all who are not free. Amen.
kids: Children, God said: Let there be light! And there was light. Everything God made is good, and you are good too! Let us say thank you to God.

homily: Dear friends, today the creation story reaches its summit: God said, let us make humankind in our image, according to our likeness (Genesis 1:26). Only of us is this said.

So God created humankind in his image, male and female he created them (Genesis 1:27). Every person bears God's image: the child in the womb, the poor man at the gate, the old woman in her bed. Then God rested on the seventh day and blessed it. Our work finds its meaning in rest and worship.

In the Gospel Jesus quotes Isaiah: this people honours me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me (Mark 7:6). Some had used religious customs to avoid caring for their own parents. Jesus says: you abandon the commandment of God and hold to human tradition (Mark 7:8).
Tomorrow is Ash Wednesday. Lent asks one thing: give God your heart, not only your lips. Let us choose tonight how we will pray, fast and give, and let God restore his image in us. Amen.
kids: Children, God made you like himself! That is why every person is special. This Lent, let us love Jesus with our hearts, not only with our words.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, Lent begins with a trumpet. The prophet Joel cries out: yet even now, says the LORD, return to me with all your heart, with fasting, with weeping, and with mourning; rend your hearts and not your clothing (Joel 2:12–13).

Why return? Not because God is harsh, but because he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love (Joel 2:13). And Joel calls everyone: elders and children, the newly married and the priests. Lent is the whole Church coming home together.

Paul pleads with us: we entreat you on behalf of Christ, be reconciled to God (2 Corinthians 5:20). He who knew no sin was made sin for us, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God. And he adds: see, now is the acceptable time; see, now is the day of salvation! Not next year. Today.

Jesus gives us three works: almsgiving, prayer and fasting. But he warns: do not do them to be seen. Give so quietly that your left hand does not know what your right hand is doing; pray in your room with the door shut; fast with a washed face. And your Father who sees in secret will reward you (Matthew 6:4, 6, 18).

In a moment we will receive ashes. The priest will say: repent, and believe in the Gospel, or: remember that you are dust, and to dust you shall return. The ashes are not a decoration. They are an honest confession: we are sinners, we are mortal, and we need God's mercy.

Yet dust in God's hands is never just dust. From dust he formed Adam; from the dust of the tomb he will raise us. Let us begin these forty days with torn-open hearts, hidden love and great hope. Amen.
kids: Children, today we get a cross of ashes on our foreheads. It reminds us that we need Jesus and that we want to love him more.
For Lent, choose one way to pray more, one thing to give up, and one way to help someone, and do it quietly for Jesus.

homily: Dear friends, Moses sets a choice before Israel: I have set before you life and death, blessings and curses. Choose life so that you and your descendants may live (Deuteronomy 30:19). Lent begins with this same choice.

Jesus shows us the road to life. The Son of Man must suffer, be rejected, be killed and on the third day be raised. Then he says to all: if any want to become my followers, let them deny themselves and take up their cross daily and follow me (Luke 9:23).

Daily. Not one great sacrifice, but small faithful choices: patience at home, honesty at work, kindness to the difficult. And Jesus asks: what does it profit them if they gain the whole world, but lose or forfeit themselves? (Luke 9:25).

Today we remember Our Lady of Lourdes and pray for the sick on the World Day of the Sick. At Lourdes Mary asked for prayer and penance. Many have been healed; many more have received strength to carry their cross. With Mary, let us choose life by following Jesus on the way of the cross. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says: carry your cross every day. That means doing hard good things with love. Mary helps us, like she helped St Bernadette at Lourdes. Let us pray for sick people today!

homily: Dear friends, God tells Isaiah: shout out, do not hold back! The people fast and complain that God does not notice. God replies: you serve your own interest on your fast day, and oppress all your workers (Isaiah 58:3).

Then God describes the fast he chooses: to loose the bonds of injustice, to let the oppressed go free, to share your bread with the hungry, and bring the homeless poor into your house (Isaiah 58:6–7). Fasting without mercy is empty.

And the promise: then your light shall break forth like the dawn; you shall call, and the LORD will answer, here I am (Isaiah 58:8–9). In the Gospel Jesus says his disciples will fast when the bridegroom is taken away (Matthew 9:15). We fast because we long for him.
On this first Friday of Lent, let our abstinence be love: for Jesus the Bridegroom, who was taken away on the cross, and for the poor in whom he waits for us. Amen.
kids: Children, God says the best kind of fasting is sharing. If we give up a sweet this Lent, let us use it to help someone who is hungry!

homily: Dear friends, Isaiah promises: if you remove the yoke from among you, the pointing of the finger, the speaking of evil, if you offer your food to the hungry, then your light shall rise in the darkness (Isaiah 58:9–10).

The Lord will guide you continually, and you shall be like a watered garden, like a spring of water, whose waters never fail (Isaiah 58:11). Small sins like gossip and blame dry us up; mercy makes us a garden.

Jesus sees Levi, a tax collector, and says: follow me. And he got up, left everything, and followed him (Luke 5:27–28). When the Pharisees complain, Jesus says: those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick; I have come to call not the righteous but sinners to repentance (Luke 5:31–32).
Lent is not for perfect people. It is for the sick who know they need the Doctor. Let us get up from wherever we are sitting, and follow Jesus, beginning with a good confession. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus called Levi, even though people did not like him, and Levi followed Jesus. Jesus is like a doctor for our hearts. When we do wrong, we can always go back to him.

The Lord comes to his temple: the offering of the poor, the light of the nations, the sword.

points.h: The Lord comes to his temple
sub: A child in his mother's arms.

points.apply: Offer your day to God every morning this week.

q: I will give you as a light to the nations, that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth.”
for my eyes have seen your salvation, which you have prepared in the presence of all peoples, a light for revelation to the Gentiles and for glory to your people Israel.”

q: He was despised and rejected by others; a man of suffering and acquainted with infirmity;
and to be a sign that will be opposed so that the inner thoughts of many will be revealed

Let us present our lives to him and carry his light.

Job's night, the healing hand of Jesus, prayer in the dark, and the urgency of the Gospel.

q: When I lie down I say, ‘When shall I rise?’ But the night is long, and I am full of tossing until dawn.

points.apply: Bring your own long night honestly to God in prayer.

points.h: He took her by the hand
q: He heals the brokenhearted, and binds up their wounds.
He came and took her by the hand and lifted her up. Then the fever left her, and she began to serve them.

sub: While it was still very dark.

In the morning, while it was still very dark, he got up and went out to a deserted place, and there he prayed.
points.apply: Give God the first ten minutes of each morning.

points.h: Woe to me if I do not proclaim
q: then within me there is something like a burning fire shut up in my bones; I am weary with holding it in, and I cannot.
If I proclaim the gospel, this gives me no ground for boasting, for an obligation is laid on me, and woe to me if I do not proclaim the gospel!
points.apply: Decide on one way to share your faith during Lent.

concl: The Lord who counts the stars binds up our wounds.
Healed by his hand, strengthened by prayer, let us serve and proclaim.
2027-02-07.resolve: Visit a sick person before the World Day of the Sick on 11 February.

intro: Theme: “The time is fulfilled… repent, and believe in the good news.”
The bow of peace, the waters of baptism, the desert of testing and the call to conversion.

q: I have set my bow in the clouds, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between me and the earth.
For in him every one of God's promises is a “Yes.”
points.apply: When you see the sky this week, thank God for his faithfulness.

sub: An appeal for a good conscience.
q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove from your body the heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
For Christ also suffered for sins once for all, the righteous for the unrighteous, in order to bring you to God. He was put to death in the flesh, but made alive in the spirit,
points.apply: Find the date of your baptism and renew your baptismal promises in prayer.

q: Remember the long way that the LORD your God has led you these forty years in the wilderness, in order to humble you, testing you to know what was in your heart, whether or not you would keep his commandments.
For we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but we have one who in every respect has been tested as we are, yet without sin.
points.apply: Name your strongest temptation and bring it to Jesus each day.

q: Make me to know your ways, O LORD; teach me your paths.
and saying, “The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has come near; repent, and believe in the good news.”
points.apply: Keep a daily desert of ten minutes' silence with the Gospel.

concl: God's covenant of peace reaches us through the waters of baptism.
Jesus has faced the desert for us; with him we can overcome.
2027-02-14.resolve: Pray each day of Lent for the elect and for your own fidelity to baptism.

intro: Theme: “Tell them how much the Lord has done for you.”
The faithful who suffered, the man made whole, and the mission that begins at home.

q: Be strong, and let your heart take courage, all you who wait for the LORD.
of whom the world was not worthy. They wandered in deserts and mountains, and in caves and holes in the ground.
points.apply: Thank God by name for one person whose faith carried yours.

sub: Clothed and in his right mind.
q: he brought them out of darkness and gloom, and broke their bonds asunder.
They came to Jesus and saw the demoniac sitting there, clothed and in his right mind, the very man who had had the legion; and they were afraid.
points.apply: Bring what divides you inside to Jesus in confession.

sub: The first missionary of the Decapolis.
q: Come and hear, all you who fear God, and I will tell what he has done for me.
But Jesus refused, and said to him, “Go home to your friends, and tell them how much the Lord has done for you, and what mercy he has shown you.”
points.apply: Tell one family member what God has done for you.

concl: Faith is faithful whether it escapes the sword or not.
Jesus makes us whole and sends us home as witnesses.
2027-02-01.resolve: Share one story of God's mercy at the family table this week.

intro: Theme: “The Lord disciplines those whom he loves.”
A Father's training, a hometown's unbelief, and faith that sees the Lord afresh.

q: for the LORD reproves the one he loves, as a father the son in whom he delights.
Now, discipline always seems painful rather than pleasant at the time, but later it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those who have been trained by it.
points.apply: Offer one present hardship to God as training in holiness.

q: he had no form or majesty that we should look at him, nothing in his appearance that we should desire him.
Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary and brother of James and Joses and Judas and Simon, and are not his sisters here with us?” And they took offense at him.
points.apply: Read the Gospel this week as if for the first time.

q: As a father has compassion for his children, so the LORD has compassion for those who fear him.
And he could do no deed of power there, except that he laid his hands on a few sick people and cured them. And he was amazed at their unbelief.
points.apply: Make an act of faith before Communion: Lord, I believe.

concl: God's discipline is a Father's love.
Let us welcome Jesus with faith, not with the familiarity that shuts him out.
2027-02-03.resolve: Pray each day this week: Lord, I believe; help my unbelief.

intro: Theme: “He began to send them out two by two.”
The festival of heaven and the mission of the Twelve.

sub: The city of the living God.
Blood that speaks a better word.
q: Now Mount Sinai was wrapped in smoke, because the LORD had descended upon it in fire; the smoke went up like the smoke of a kiln, while the whole mountain shook violently.
But you have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to innumerable angels in festal gathering,
points.apply: At Mass this week, join consciously in the song of the angels at the Holy, Holy.

q: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news,
He called the twelve and began to send them out two by two, and gave them authority over the unclean spirits.
points.apply: Do one act of service together with a friend.

q: We ponder your steadfast love, O God, in the midst of your temple.
So they went out and proclaimed that all should repent. They cast out many demons, and anointed with oil many who were sick and cured them.
points.apply: Visit or call someone who is sick.

concl: At Mass we stand on Zion with angels and saints.
From Mass we are sent, together and trusting, to heal.
2027-02-04.resolve: Visit a sick or lonely person with a companion this week.

intro: Theme: “Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.”
Mutual love, the Lord who never leaves, and the courage of John and St Agatha.

sub: Free from the love of money.
q: you shall love the alien as yourself, for you were aliens in the land of Egypt
Let mutual love continue. Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers, for by doing that some have entertained angels without knowing it.
points.apply: Welcome one stranger or newcomer this week.

points.h: The same yesterday, today and forever
q: The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? The LORD is the stronghold of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.
points.apply: Repeat Hebrews 13:8 whenever you feel afraid.

sub: Trapped by an oath and guests.
q: Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to deliver you, says the LORD.”
For John had been telling Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife.”
points.apply: Refuse one compromise made only to please others.

concl: Love, hospitality and courage flow from a Lord who never changes.
Like John and St Agatha, let us fear God more than people.
2027-02-05.resolve: Ask St Agatha each day this week for courage and purity of heart.

intro: Theme: “He had compassion for them.”
Praise and sharing, rest with Jesus, and the compassion of the Good Shepherd seen in the martyrs of Nagasaki.

q: Offer to God a sacrifice of thanksgiving, and pay your vows to the Most High.
Through him, then, let us continually offer a sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of lips that confess his name.
points.apply: Begin and end each day with a short act of praise.

q: He makes me lie down in green pastures; he leads me beside still waters; he restores my soul.
He said to them, “Come away to a deserted place all by yourselves and rest a while.” For many were coming and going, and they had no leisure even to eat.
points.apply: Keep Sunday as a day of rest with the Lord.

q: I myself will be the shepherd of my sheep, and I will make them lie down, says the Lord GOD.
As he went ashore, he saw a great crowd; and he had compassion for them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd; and he began to teach them many things.
points.apply: Pray for persecuted Christians in Asia, through St Paul Miki.

concl: Our praise and sharing are the sacrifice God desires.
The Good Shepherd gives rest and compassion; the martyrs show the cost of love.
2027-02-06.resolve: Make Sunday a true day of rest and praise this week.

intro: Theme: “All who touched it were healed.”
The good Creator who speaks light into darkness, and the Word made flesh whose touch heals.

q: Then God said, “Let there be light”; and there was light.
For it is the God who said, “Let light shine out of darkness,” who has shone in our hearts to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.
points.apply: Begin each day this week with a short prayer of light: Lord, shine in my heart.

q: O LORD, how manifold are your works! In wisdom you have made them all; the earth is full of your creatures.
Ever since the creation of the world his eternal power and divine nature, invisible though they are, have been understood and seen through the things he has made.
points.apply: Waste less this week: food, water or electricity, as a thank-you to the Creator.

q: But he was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities; upon him was the punishment that made us whole, and by his bruises we are healed.
And wherever he went, into villages or cities or farms, they laid the sick in the marketplaces, and begged him that they might touch even the fringe of his cloak; and all who touched it were healed.
points.apply: Visit, call or pray for one sick person by name.

concl: The world is the good gift of a good God.
In Jesus the Creator walks among us and heals.
2027-02-08.resolve: Thank God for one created thing every day this week.

intro: Theme: “Their hearts are far from me.”
Made in God's image, called to worship with the heart, on the eve of Lent.

sub: Only of us is it said.
q: So God created humankind in his image, in the image of God he created them; male and female he created them.
For we are what he has made us, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand to be our way of life.
points.apply: Show special respect this week to someone the world overlooks.

q: So God blessed the seventh day and hallowed it, because on it God rested from all the work that he had done in creation.
So then, a sabbath rest still remains for the people of God;
points.apply: Keep next Sunday free for Mass, family and rest.

q: Honor your father and your mother, so that your days may be long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
He said to them, “Isaiah prophesied rightly about you hypocrites, as it is written, ‘This people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me;
points.apply: Do one concrete act of care for your parents or elders this week.

concl: We bear God's image; let our worship come from the heart.
Lent begins tomorrow: return to God with the heart.
2027-02-09.resolve: Write down your Lenten resolutions of prayer, fasting and almsgiving tonight.

intro: Theme: “Return to me with all your heart.”
Ash Wednesday: the torn heart, the urgent now, the hidden works, and the dust that God loves.

q: Return to the LORD, your God, for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love, and relents from punishing.
So he set off and went to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was filled with compassion; he ran and put his arms around him and kissed him.
points.apply: Name one sin you will bring to confession this week.

q: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and put a new and right spirit within me.
For he says, “At an acceptable time I have listened to you, and on a day of salvation I have helped you.” See, now is the acceptable time; see, now is the day of salvation!
points.apply: Do today the act of reconciliation you have been postponing.

q: Prayer with fasting is good, but better than both is almsgiving with righteousness.
But whenever you pray, go into your room and shut the door and pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.
points.apply: Keep one Lenten practice that no one else will know about.

q: By the sweat of your face you shall eat bread until you return to the ground, for out of it you were taken; you are dust, and to dust you shall return.”
Therefore we have been buried with him by baptism into death, so that, just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, so we too might walk in newness of life.
points.apply: Each night of Lent, pray: Lord, I am dust; have mercy and make me new.

concl: Lent is the whole Church returning to a gracious Father.
We are dust, but dust in the hands of the God who raises the dead.
2027-02-10.resolve: Write your three Lenten works and keep them daily, in secret.

intro: Theme: “Choose life.”
Two ways, the daily cross, and Mary of Lourdes beside the sick.

sub: Life and death set before us.
q: I call heaven and earth to witness against you today that I have set before you life and death, blessings and curses. Choose life so that you and your descendants may live,
I came that they may have life, and have it abundantly.
points.apply: Each morning of Lent, say: today I choose life; today I choose you, Lord.

sub: The Son of Man must suffer.
q: They are like trees planted by streams of water, which yield their fruit in its season, and their leaves do not wither. In all that they do, they prosper.
Then he said to them all, “If any want to become my followers, let them deny themselves and take up their cross daily and follow me.
points.apply: Name your daily cross and carry it with love this week.

q: As a mother comforts her child, so I will comfort you; you shall be comforted in Jerusalem.
Meanwhile, standing near the cross of Jesus were his mother,
points.apply: Visit or call a sick person this week, and pray a decade of the Rosary for them.

concl: God sets before us life; Jesus shows the way through the cross.
Mary stands with us and with the sick.
2027-02-11.resolve: Offer one daily cross for the sick throughout this week.

intro: Theme: “Is not this the fast that I choose?”
The fast God wants: justice, mercy and longing for the Bridegroom.

q: Look, you fast only to quarrel and to fight and to strike with a wicked fist. Such fasting as you do today will not make your voice heard on high.
Those who say, “I love God,” and hate their brothers or sisters, are liars;
points.apply: Examine how you treat those who work for you or under you.

sub: Do not hide from your own kin.
q: Is it not to share your bread with the hungry, and bring the homeless poor into your house; when you see the naked, to cover them, and not to hide yourself from your own kin?
for I was hungry and you gave me food, I was thirsty and you gave me something to drink, I was a stranger and you welcomed me,
points.apply: Give what you save by fasting to the poor this week.

q: And I will take you for my wife forever; I will take you for my wife in righteousness and in justice, in steadfast love, and in mercy.
And Jesus said to them, “The wedding guests cannot mourn as long as the bridegroom is with them, can they? The days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast.
points.apply: When hunger comes today, turn it into a short prayer: Come, Lord Jesus.

concl: True fasting breaks yokes and shares bread.
We fast in love for the Bridegroom and his poor.
2027-02-12.resolve: Keep the Fridays of Lent with abstinence and one act of sharing.

intro: Theme: “I have come to call… sinners to repentance.”
Mercy that makes us a garden, and the Physician who calls the sick.

q: If you remove the yoke from among you, the pointing of the finger, the speaking of evil,
Do not judge, so that you may not be judged.
points.apply: Replace every criticism today with a prayer for that person.

q: The LORD will guide you continually, and satisfy your needs in parched places, and make your bones strong; and you shall be like a watered garden, like a spring of water, whose waters never fail.
The water that I will give will become in them a spring of water gushing up to eternal life.”
points.apply: Do one act of mercy that repairs a broken relationship.

q: I myself will be the shepherd of my sheep, and I will make them lie down, says the Lord GOD. I will seek the lost, and I will bring back the strayed, and I will bind up the injured, and I will strengthen the weak,
Jesus answered, “Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick; I have come to call not the righteous but sinners to repentance.”
points.apply: Go to confession before the Second Sunday of Lent.

concl: Mercy turns a dry life into a watered garden.
Jesus calls sinners; Lent is for the sick who need him.
2027-02-13.resolve: Give up gossip and criticism for the whole of Lent.
